page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-16 is a high-memory general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz on an Intel Xeon platform. Cache sizing includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a 45 MB shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 104.0 GB, delivering 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest per-core throughput combined with stable multithreaded capacity. In stress-ng, single-core CPU throughput registers 1,113.69 points, positioning it in the bottom 25%, while multi-core processing reaches 11,743.65 points. A similar pattern appears in Geekbench, where the single-core score of 937.0 ranks in the weak tier, contrasting with a multi-core score of 5,935.0. Data compression tests reveal constraints on older instruction pipelines, reflected in single-threaded gzip compression at 18.85 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 7.15 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 10%. Extended instruction capability includes AVX and AES support, but modern instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX are not present.

Memory subsystem testing shows uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 81.5 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaching 43.43 GB/sec, alongside a cached small-block bandwidth of 646.32 GB/sec. Application testing displays consistent middle-tier behavior, with Redis processing 10.99 million SET operations per second, static web serving throughput reaching 9.64 GB/sec, and the PassMark database operations metric logging 4,982.36. Large language model execution is functional on smaller architectures, hitting 165.21 tokens per second on a 135M model, but drops to 10.38 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

Qualitatively, the hardware offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for configurations that require large working sets without demanding peak per-core processing rates. Because persistent disk storage must be provisioned externally and single-threaded execution speeds lag newer CPU generations, the instance is best deployed for in-memory databases, medium-scale caching layers, and memory-heavy enterprise backend services.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-16 is an x86_64 instance configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.3 GHz and 104.0 GB of memory. It features no local disk storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations show moderate multi-core performance alongside lower single-core throughput, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,935.0 and single-core score of 937.0. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression test in the lower tier, whereas memory bandwidth delivers 81.5 GB/sec for uncached read operations. The instance demonstrates solid throughput in memory-bound operations, achieving 10.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.64 GB/sec in static web serving. The elevated memory ratio of 6.5 GB per vCPU makes it well suited for in-memory caching systems, database engines, and medium-scale backend analytics that do not rely on high single-threaded CPU speed.
